citationText: I. Godor et al., “A Look Inside 5G Standards to Support Time Synchronization for Smart Manufacturing,” IEEE Commun. Standards Mag., 4(3):14–21, Sep. 2020, doi: 10.1109/ MCOMSTD.001.2000010. Accessed: Nov. 19, 2022. [Online]. Available: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9204594Release 17, 3GPP added additional PTP functionalities, such as enabling the 5G system to act as a TC. This paper first presented an evaluation setup for systematically evaluating the time synchronization precision between a wireless device and a wired PTP Grandmaster. The article presented results, focusing on the technical feasibility of precise time synchronization over a wireless link. The evaluation showed that a synchronization accuracy of less than 4 μs can be achieved with residence time measured and reported by the 5G system compared to ~120–150 μs without the 5G network inserting the residence time. The accuracy difference between the linear regression and PI servo with additional tweaks was negligible. Therefore, based on these results, a more hassle-free linear regression servo can be used whenever available without any performance degradation. These results prove the possibility of using such a system for conventional media production over 5G, where the genlock or sampling references are generated locally by a media device receiving the timing information from a network via PTP. For high-performance uncompressed media like the ST 2110 and the precise packet pacing required by the ST 2110-21, the reported accuracy is insufficient in the current technological iteration. However, it is unlikely that uncompressed video will be transported over a 5G network due to radio spectrum availability. In summary, the authors still believe that the results appear promising for potential use for compressed solutions. Upcoming iterations of the 5G spec introducing additional timing and media-specific functionality and improved high-efficiency low latency encoding technologies may ensure such use cases. Future experiments may look closer at the precision of the offset measurements through the 5G systems and additional practical use cases using various compression technologies.
title: A Look Inside 5G Standards to Support Time Synchronization for Smart Manufacturing
